fieldMarks: More obvious pale bars on the tail feathers and a longer plume on the back of the head.
Displaying males puff out a white chest and inflate yellow air sacs; males slightly larger than females.
behavior: Displaying male gives 9–10 low hooting gobbles with wing sounds, very different from the greater sage-grouse display.
Fall and winter diet may be almost entirely sagebrush leaves and shoots; also flowers, buds and summer insects.
habitat: Sagebrush plains and high valleys; nesting habitat includes lower wet areas where young forage for insects.
range: Year-round resident of southwestern Colorado and adjacent Utah only; gone from about 90 percent of its former range.

lookalikes.name: Greater sage-grouse
lookalikes.howToTell: Greater is larger, with a different display and fainter tail bars; the ranges do not overlap.
